review_text: My parents live in Howell and I looooooove to eat here... but I live an hour away and I have searched and searched for places even 1/2 as good as Los Tres Amigos to no avail.  This place just can't be beat.  Even Mexican Town in Detroit is no match.  The lunch prices at Los Tres are especially good.  The fajittas are to die for.  You get free chips and salsa, food comes out fast and hot, and I've always had good service.  This place is honestly amazing.

I grew up in Texas, where my favorite food was Tex-Mex.  Although that's fairly stereotypical, I think it says a lot for my point of view.  Anyway, this is by far the best Tex-Mex I've had in a long, long time.  It's top notch, it's fairly quick, and reasonably priced.  I have been here twice; two weeks in a row.  I love it!  The hot sauce on the table is actually hot, the chips are great, the enchiladas are wonderful as is the fajita taco salad.  Great place!

Los Tres has a great wait staff and tasty food.  If you want a pitcher of Dos Equis and some great mexican chow with some friends, this is the place.  I've eaten here about a dozen times and the only time service was slow I was with a rather large group.
Service is very fast, food is good. Never been there for a game day, but they have many TV's. Monday nights they seem to be very busy, maybe a drink special?

Bad lunch, I got a chile relleno with a taco, my wife had seafood fajitas.  My taco tasted like really bad quality canned meat, which the waitress was kind enough to take back and replace with a chicken taco, which was at least edible, though still not good.  My chile relleno was good, but my wife was too polite to say anything about her seafood, she mentioned to me in the restaurant that it was fake krab, which I thought was OK, but when she got in the car she said the shrimp tasted really bad and she felt sick after eating a little bit of it, even though she brought the rest home as leftovers.  We will not go back.

I had been going here for years, and the service has always been poor, something my friends and I overlook because we enjoy the food so much. Our most recent experience left us all speechless. We were overcharged, and the manager and server were the most rude service people I've ever encountered; not just in a restaurant, but anywhere. From the minute we walked in, we were treated in a hostile way by the server, who couldn't understand anything we were saying. As a result of this, we received things that we didn't order, and didn't receive things we actually ordered. When I approached the manager, he said that "there are other places I can go". He had no interest in accommodating us, and frankly, I feel like he was making up policies on the spot. Worst restaurant experience of my life. Never go to a Los Tres if you can help it.

Went to check out the new Mexican restaurant on the block, as we usually go to Old Mexico just east on 5 mile. Took my wife and two teen girls that just love Mexican food. The girls ordered a nacho platter, my wife ordered a chicken burrito, and I decided to try the Beef tacos.
We ordered Margaritas that were basically weak lime juice and a scoop of ice, so we sent them back for bottled beer. Easy to get that right. When our food came after a long wait, it was cold, the nacho platter had cold, grated cheese on it, and a mound of shreeded lettuce on top that you had to dig through to get to the chips, like some demented, corn chip salad. Most disheartening.
My wife was had the most quizzical look on her face after every other bite, as if she couldnt believe what she was tasting, so I tried a bite. The flavor could only be described as vaguely chicken, with an overpowering cilantro flavor that she kept drowning in hot sauce to make palatable.
As stated before, I recieved room temperature beef tacos, with grease saturated shells, with cheese and warm, flaccid lettuce, similar to the consistency of microwaved taco bell, which certainly has them beat in the flavor and price department. The girls joked that we would've been better served there, especially since it is just next door. If you are contemplating going here, I would recommend grab some Taco bell, and sit in Los tres Amigos for the ambience. Its the only thing they have going for them.

Tonight, before I made my hour commute from work back home to Chelsea, I called ahead to double check the closing time. The friendly voice told me 10pm. I arrived at 8pm. "table for 1 please" the hostess grabbed a menu, and started to walk me to a table. A gentlemen came out from behind the bar, and made a strange hand gestures, similar to a baseball umpire. He told her "no!" - and she then said to me "I guess we are not seating anyone right now"

I am also 5ft 11, tattooed, have a beard (well manicured every 7 days by a barber) and weigh 230lbs mostly lean mass. (I body build)

I will never visit Los Tres Amigos again. If you check my review history, I travel often and make it a point to leave POSITIVE reviews every where I go. This business is new to our city. I wish them no ill will, but I sincerely hope they see this review, and learn from this experience.

Expensive, Mediocre Food. Inflexible, Horrible Carry Out Service.

Living close by, Los Tres in Mason was our go-to place; we were regulars ordering 2-4 times a month for a family of four until we stopped going a couple years ago. Last night we decided to try it again and ordered carry out...and again I was profoundly disappointed. Food was just ok (fajitas had tons of peppers and onions with little meat, we even ordered the double meat dinner). The kicker was they refused to give us any hot salsa, even in place of the mild salsa, unless we paid $1.95 for a salad dressing cup size of it. There is hot salsa sitting on the tables free to seated patrons, so we asked if we could get a container for it and they said that would cost us $2 for the empty container. We quit going here after the carry out service got horrible—expensive, inflexible service, and long waits. (I'll wait an hour+ if I know it's an hour+...I don't want to go to the restaurant when they say 20 mins. and then wait an additional 40 for my take out.) In the past, they not only charged outrageously for a small container of hot salsa, the final straw was when they charged $3 for 3 corn tortillas to eat with Camarones a la Diabla (it's a saucy shrimp dish for $14). The other 20+ Mexican restaurants I have ever ordered that dish have included the tortillas with the dinner! Los Tres hasn't changed. I gave them another chance, only to still be disappointed and frustrated.

review_text:
As a recommendation, I ordered the Quesabirria and it was probably the greasiest, least flavorful tacos I have ever had. I am not sure if they are deep fried or fried on a black top grill but they were just greasy. The beef had no flavor and I actually had to add fresh jalapeno to the tacos for any type of flavor. The tacos were served room temperature as well. The sauces that came with it were just as bad. The green sauce was like baby food and bland, the red sauce was as if someone added hot sauce and sugar to ketchup, and the other sauce (consommé?) that is served in a larger ramekin was oily with added onion and cilantro. The only reason that I finished my meal was it was the only thing that I had all day minus some strawberry yoghurt for breakfast. Thank God for the chips and salsa that were on the table. Maybe make the salsa less sweet, because it tasted like salsa from a container from Sysco or US Foods.
Mind you, I was with a party of about 15 but there should be no excuse for sitting at a restaurant for at least 2 hours before receiving our meals. The service was so bad that we saw people just get up and leave after sitting at their own tables for a while. I felt bad for our waitress telling us that they were understaffed, and she was supposed to already be off of her shift so she was trying to do the best that she could, but I wouldn't want my staff voicing their frustrations to customers.
I have tried Los Tres Amigos before, and honestly this place is not any better than the first time. I love Tex-Mex and Mexican food being that I am originally from Texas, so I grew up eating this type of food weekly and I also make it from scratch at home (no kits, cans or packaged seasoning). I can honestly tell you that I would not recommend or even classify Los Tres Amigos as Tex-Mex or Mexican. I am being harsh on this but this is my honest opinion on spending over $50 for 2 meals.

review_text:
I have been to my fair share of Mexican restaurants in Jackson by now and this one really takes the cake (or should I say "Tres Leches Cake"). Don't let this little shack of a building crammed onto the smallest lot on Michigan Ave. with an underwhelming sign pass you by. The food was phenomenal and prices were beyond reasonable!

The food variety itself was a typical Mexican restaurant variety, which means you have a plethora of chicken, steak, chorizo, and vegetarian options. And like most Mexican restaurants, the menu is flashy and a tad intense for the uninitiated. This isn't a ding against the restaurant since it is the norm for this genre.

I ordered a large burrito, thinking it was going to be a larger burrito. But no, was I wrong. Way wrong. This burrito filled my plate and some. It was so large and the price was so cheap (I think around $10, if that), and so good that I literally thought I was stealing. I also ordered a margaritas because it was happy hour and it was one of the only times that someone/someplace made tequila good.

The only reason I can't give 5/5 stars is because the service was uncharacteristically slow. We sat for about 10 minutes after eating, waiting for a check. I believe they were preparing for a birthday party later and it truly wasn't that big of a deal, but I rate all restaurants on the same measuring stick, so no difference here.

TL;DR - Phenomenal food, great prices, friendly, yet slow service. Completely worth your money.

Has anyone else over 65 been carded here or anywhere else? ...and refused service because they were not driving, thus having no need to carry their wallet?

review_text:
My very first time at Los Tres Amigos will also be my very last. I have a severe peanut allergy and I ordered an enchilada thinking, as always, that's a safe choice. I've ordered enchiladas at numerous Mexican restaurants without ever having any issues. I began eating and immediately had a reaction. We called the waitress over and asked about peanuts. She asked the cooks who said, "it's possible that it's in the sauce". There is no warning about peanuts on the menu (which I discovered is not legally mandatory). Luckily I'm fine, thanks to my daughter's quick trip to get Benadryl. My worry is that others with a peanut allergy may experience the same reaction or worse. The server and the person I assumed to be the manager showed no sympathy whatsoever. After talking to the manager while paying the bill* and explaining that I was worried about other people with peanut allergies worse than mine, his only response was that I should've informed the server. He's right, but in all the years I've eaten enchiladas, not once did I worry about peanuts. Lesson learned. I wish Los Tres Amigos would learn a lesson too: Warn your customers about peanuts, it could cost someone their life.

*I still had to pay for my meal and was not given any kind of apology from the manager.

review_text:
Delicious Mexican food... generally above average and basically top-notch for Michigan.  I have traveled to maybe 20 Mexican restaurants in Michigan looking for even reasonable Mexican food, and this is about as good as I've found.  Sagebrush in Lake Orion does a nice fajita, and there is a small taco place on 10 mile in South Lyon called Two Tostadas.  And that is about it.

We've been here 4 times since moving back to Northville a month ago.  The menu is amazingly reasonably priced for Northville, or really for anywhere.  The tacos have been excellent, the common Mexican sides are pretty standard, but the roasted onions that come with the 3 taco platter are pretty good.  Side salsa with the meals is suitably spicy, main salsa with chips when you sit down is more mild.

The service is polite and fast, and we have had very few issues.  A drink arrived after our meal last time we ate there, and they comped it - honestly, the manager coming over to apologize would have been enough, mostly you just want to see that someone gives a *** these days, as so many places seem not to.

If you're used to southern Mexican food (e.g., Texas), this is the closest you're going to get.  The place is not huge, so maybe call ahead, but it's definitely worth the stop.  I didn't realize they had more than one location, so I'm only vouching for the one in Northville, haven't been to the others.

This is my absolute go-to restaurant. I’d say we’ve been here probably 2-3 times a month for at least the last year and it’s never once disappointed.

Both my husband and I have a standing order— a chimichanga (I prefer the chicken, he gets the shredded beef) and an order of the queso fundido. Service has always been great (ironically the only time it was off was the first time we came but the food was good enough to bring us back and the waitstaff has been amazing since) and the restaurant is incredibly clean.

Their lunch hours are, I believe 11am - 2pm (possibly starts at noon?) and we generally try to go then but we’ve even stopped in an hour before closing on weekdays for just apps and dessert and were still happy with our visit. The soda can be a little persnickety so I generally get water but my husband enjoys their fountain drinks.

I know they have a large selection of alcoholic beverages but we’re not a drinking family so I can’t comment on that. I will say I often see other tables with fancy, pretty looking drinks so they must be of a good quality as well. We have kids who don’t enjoy Mexican cuisine and they’ve ordered the chicken tenders and fries 3+ times and each time, commented on how it’s “real chicken” and really enjoyed their meals.

I was craving birria tacos tonight, so I headed straight to the restaurant's website to place my order. I was going to be picking the order up, so I figured it would be easier to order directly through the restaurant rather than through a delivery app. Excitedly, I ordered three servings of their birria tacos, along with sides of rice and beans for each order. However, upon arriving home and delving into our meal, we discovered that the rice and beans were missing. Disappointed but hopeful for a quick resolution, I called the restaurant, expecting a simple refund for the missing sides. We had already eaten, so obviously we no longer needed the sides. I assumed it would be no problem for them to just issue me a refund – even if I had to come pick the refund up.

Unfortunately, the situation quickly escalated into a frustrating ordeal. Despite them acknowledging their mistake, they refused to issue a refund. Instead, the guy on the phone argued with me about it, offered to only give me ONE order of rice and beans (out of the THREE that I had ordered… which is WILD), and then subsequently hung up on me! Extremely unprofessional. I was not yelling or rude to him; he simply did not want to handle the situation, and just hung up!

My following in-person visit didn’t make things any better. While the woman I spoke with in person was nicer than the guy over the phone, there was still a lack of willingness to rectify THEIR error. She stated that my order had gone through “Bento Box'' and did not come directly through them, so that was the reason they could not refund me. I still fail to see how that’s MY problem when I ordered directly from the restaurant’s website. Whatever partnership they may have with Bento Box has zero to do with me. They are obviously still going to receive my money one way or another, it’s not like they fed me out of the kindness of their hearts. So I still don’t understand why they would refuse to issue a refund, regardless of which platform my order went through. At this point, I think it would’ve actually been easier to have ordered through a delivery app. At least I could have requested a refund.

On top of that, despite them having my order in black-and-white right in front of them, it still took ten minutes of explanation for them to finally realize that I actually ordered (and PAID for) THREE sides instead of just ONE. Apparently, since all of the orders were for the exact same thing, they somehow missed the fact that the order said “x3”, which means I ordered THREE of the same thing. Either the employees need to be trained on this, or their website checkout needs to be redesigned. It’s ridiculous that I had to PROVE what I ordered and paid for. review_text:
UPDATE: We've been to Mi Lindo San Blas several times now. The last time, they seemed to have had an off night.  The seviche was completely bland. It seemed fresh enough, but definitely not marinated in lime juice. I would also stay away from their oysters. They were not fresh at all and had a terrible taste... I couldn't even swallow it. Brought it up to the waitress, and she mentioned others have said the same. I really hope they take action to correct these issues. Otherwise, we will likely not be back.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: This was our first time visiting Mi Lindo San Blas. Upon entering, you're greeted by lovely murals all over the walls. The space is fairly small but inviting. We were seated promptly, and the waitress immediately took our drink order. We ordered a Long Island and a Michelada, which were a bit pricey ($9.99) but delicious.

For appetizer, we got the shrimp seviche. It was very fresh and delicious... finally, I have a go-to for my seviche cravings! For the main course, my partner got a beef burrito, and I got a whole red snapper Nayarit style. The burrito was very good, but that snapper stole the show! The skin was crispy, but the meat was flakey and tender. Nayarit style sauce added a lot of flavor and just a hint of heat... very tasty. The freshness of the food was apparent, and I hope this never changes.

All in all, a great experience. The food and the ambiance actually reminded me of being back in Mexico.

review_text:
I've adjusted my rating down to 1 star at this point.

After posting my original review, I received a response asking me to reach out so they could make things right. I did exactly that on June 3rd, and as of today, June 8th, I have not received any response or follow-up.

Unfortunately, the lack of communication and customer service has made it clear that our business is not valued. I sincerely hope you take steps to improve the experience for future guests; otherwise, you may continue to lose customers. To make matters worse, all of this stems from a $45 crab meal and one additional entrée. After leaving a generous tip, our total came to approximately $85. Based on this experience and the way the situation has been handled, we will not be ordering from this establishment again. Take care.

Update 5/31/2026
I've decided to update my review because I feel the quality of this restaurant has declined.

Ever since I first tried the crab legs, I've been a loyal customer, ordering them at least once a month. Up until now, they've been consistently good. This time, however, I placed an online order and was very disappointed. When I opened my meal, the sauce tasted completely different than usual. It was extremely oily, lacked flavor, and did not resemble what I've received in the past.

I also paid for extra cucumbers but received very few. Despite tipping well and spending approximately $85 on the order, the overall experience fell far short of expectations.

I called the restaurant right away and was told that the cooks prepared the meal the same way they always do. I explained that the taste was noticeably off, but my concerns weren't really addressed. I then spent several days trying to reach someone and wasn't able to speak with anyone until three days later.

At first, it seemed like the situation would be resolved with a replacement meal. Instead, I was offered a discount on a future order. As someone who has consistently supported this business, recommended it to friends and family, and returned month after month, being offered only a discount felt disappointing and dismissive.

I don't enjoy leaving negative reviews, especially for a place I've genuinely enjoyed for so long, but this experience left me feeling undervalued as a loyal customer.

Staying in Jackson area for a couple weeks and needed a quick bite after the gym. Saw the sign exiting the highway and decided to give it a try over Arby’s or some other fast food that was close by on Michigan Ave. When given the opportunity I prefer to spend my money with a local establishment than something I can find at home, glad Los Tres was open.

Parking is ample in this strip mall. Restaurant was very clean(an employee was actually cleaning when I entered). Friday special is $2 tacos, and although I do like a deal, I decided to skip the shells and order a burrito bowl. They have a few choices for protein, I went with Birria which was an up-charge. The food was good, $12 out the door meat was flavorful, and very much similar to your national chain bowl. Guacamole and queso are add on charges as well. Over all I think the food was quite good and reasonably priced. I may come back next Friday and try the tacos and some of the assortment of salsas as I only went with a medium salsa on my bowl and it was good, although maybe not the flavor profile I was looking for, think it was more of a smoky chipotle style. I definitely will come back. Not sure about all the negative reviews but my experience was good.  Young man making my bowl was kind, attentive, and made me aware of any possible up-charges with menu choices.

When we walked in, nostalgia took hold of me. This is the first Mexican restaurant that made me think back to my childhood and walking the streets of Mexico. The amazing scent greets you at the door!
We were greeted and seated immediately, which surprised me for a Saturday night. Chips and salsa arrived shortly after that. The chips were hot and fresh and the salsa was delicious.
We started with a guacamole appetizer which was very good. It's one of the only guacamole appetizers that we didn't need to salt; it had enough of its own flavor.
My margarita was delicious and huge.
I had a really hard time deciding what to order. (Thank you patient server! The poor guy had to come back like three times. 🤣). There's so much to choose from on the menu!
I ended up selecting the burrito and enchilada special. I was very hesitant to order this in case I didn't like their chicken, but I worried for nothing. It was very delicious! I also had plenty left over.
My husband got the Big Burrito Amigos with steak. He ate the whole thing! He was a bit disappointed that it didn't come with rice and beans but the menu did not indicate that it did.
Overall, I feel the portions were generous, the prices were very fair, the service and food were amazing. 10/10 will be back. Soon.

I wasnt going to rate but it popped up asking me to so...

We called ahead to see about making a reservation and were told they don't take reservations, but 9 people wouldn't be an issue. We arrived at 430 and they thought we were a reservation they had for 11 people at 6pm I let them know we were not and hadn't made a reservation as we were told they didn't take them when we had called a few hours ago.  We were seated and the young women acted like we were a burden right from the begining. The other waiter and the blonde waitress acted very differently to their tables, happy and checked in on them, so it didnt seem like the whole atmosphere was negative. Our waitress, she just seemed put off by us the whole time and didn't really check back. I gave my daughter my drink since our waitress didn't come check on things. The blonde waitress seemed to notice because she asked if we needed anything and we did get refills and napkins.  It was awkward and I will just go to mason from now on. Hopefully the young women was having an off day, but she definitely made it uncomfortable. We just tried to eat and get out. There was talk of leaving a lower tip and we decided to still tip well due to the holidays and hope it could raise the grumpy lady's spirits so she might act nicer to her next table.
If we go back I will speak up and just leave if need be, we just didn't want to further dampen the spirits for the birthday girl.

I will add we didn't bring any outside food like cupcakes, balloons or anything to be in the way etc. My daughter got birthday cards and one small gift.  I made sure we ordered before letting her open the cards so we wouldn't hold up the restaurant.

review_text:
This place is pretty good. I've eaten and drank here multiple times now and thought it was decent. The atmosphere is really cool. It is a little pricey though.

The first couple of times visiting here I just drank. I ordered the pina colada and it tasted very good but it was $11 if I remember correctly. So the mixed drinks and cocktails are little pricey. Just keep that in mind.

With that said, the food is a bit pricey also, specifically their seafood. If you go during lunchtime, their regular non-seafood dishes are priced reasonably. Also, their happy hour beer prices aren't too expensive either.

While the seafood here is quite expensive, the quality is pretty good. I ordered the shrimp quesadilla, as it was one of the most affordable seafood items in the menu. The cheese wasn't that good but the shrimp was excellent. I did get the squid the last time I was here and I can honestly say that it wasn't that good and the portion was very small for the price.

As for their regular dishes (non-seafood), they're okay. Their cheese isn't that good though. It kind of reminds me of cheese wiz.

I do like the variety of sauces that they have. When we first started going, they would give us complimentary ceviche. The last time we were in though, they did not. They said we could order it as an appetizer. I don't know if that was a promotional thing or what. Either way, it was appreciated and it was pretty good.

The atmosphere is pretty cool in here also, as before mentioned. The walls and ceiling are painted blue and there are paintings of fish. It feels like you are under the sea.

Overall, this place is decent. It's quite pricey for their seafood dishes but it is high quality. There regular dishes are okay. It's probably best to go during happy hour if you plan to drink. The decor of this place is quite vibrant also.

review_text:
During a recent visit to Los Tres Amigos in Livonia with my Wife and Daughter I found the experience underwhelming. While the food arrived quickly—within 8–10 minutes—the overall quality and flavor were disappointing.

I ordered a combination meal that included a tostada and a burrito, but neither lived up to expectations. The tostada was especially unappetizing—it tasted like it had been soaked in oil and then fried in oil that seemed old and overused. Instead of being crisp and flavorful, it was heavy, greasy, and unpleasant to eat. The burrito wasn’t much better, as the beef lacked seasoning, making the entire dish bland and forgettable. To make matters worse, the food was served warm rather than hot, which only added to the feeling that it wasn’t freshly prepared.

The service, while not unfriendly, was barely present. Aside from taking our order and dropping off the check, the staff didn’t check in or offer refills. It felt like we were on our own the entire meal.

Mexican cuisine should be rich, bold, and full of flavor, but that was completely missing here. With so many other dining options in the area, I was expecting something far better. Unless improvements are made in both food quality and attentiveness, I don’t see myself returning anytime soon.

review_text:
After living on Division for over four years, my fiancé and I finally decided to give Casa Tequila a try — and regretted it almost immediately. From the moment we were seated, things went downhill. We were served stale chips with salsa that tasted like it came from a can — and not even a good one. I’ve had better salsa straight out of a grocery store jar.

My fiancé ordered a skinny margarita that somehow cost $20. Twenty dollars — for a basic drink. We ordered the standard fish tacos (bland), another kind of fish taco (also forgettable), and the quesabirria tacos (just okay). And for over $20 for three underwhelming tacos? Insane.

To try to justify the price, they serve the tacos on a ridiculously oversized 12-by-8-inch wooden plank that makes no sense. It looks more like a novelty cutting board than a plate. It’s clearly meant to create a false sense of presentation value, but when the tacos don’t even come with rice or beans, it just ends up being a giant slab of wood taking up 10% of your table for no reason.

Service didn’t help the experience. When I asked for the check, the server didn’t print one — instead, he brought over a handheld scanner and awkwardly held it up with pre-set tip options. I always tip 20%, and I did — but I’ve never felt more ripped off walking out of a restaurant.

This place clearly leans heavily on branding and aesthetics, because the food and value just aren’t there. I’ll be shocked if this establishment manages to stay open for another two years. There’s no way anyone who actually lives on this street would ever come back — especially not for overpriced takeout.

If you’re craving steak and a proper cocktail, go to Gibsons — you’ll spend less and enjoy it more. And if you’re in the mood for Mexican, just about any other spot within five miles will offer better food, better pricing, and a more authentic experience — without the gimmicks.

review_text:
Casa Tequila Chicago: A Mixed Plate of Flavors and Service
Casa Tequila in Chicago offers a vibrant atmosphere that initially promises an authentic Mexican dining experience. Stepping inside, the decor is inviting, creating a lively backdrop for a meal with friends or family.
On the culinary front, the restaurant truly shines. The food at Casa Tequila is undeniably good, delivering on flavor and portion size. From classic tacos to more elaborate entrees, each dish we sampled showcased fresh ingredients and satisfying preparation. The guacamole was a particular highlight, fresh and perfectly seasoned, hinting at the quality of the main courses.
However, the experience was tempered by the service, which was merely "okay." While our server was polite, there was a noticeable lack of attentiveness and promptness. Drink refills were slow, and it took a bit longer than ideal to get their attention for requests. It wasn't poor service, but it certainly didn't elevate the dining experience.
The biggest letdown, unfortunately, came from the drinks. Despite the restaurant's name, the margaritas and other cocktails we tried fell short. They lacked the vibrancy and balance one expects from a dedicated tequila establishment, often tasting watered down or overly sweet. This was a significant disappointment, especially given the expectation of quality beverages.
In summary, Casa Tequila is a decent spot for a tasty Mexican meal in Chicago, boasting a good kitchen. While the service is acceptable, and the drinks leave much to be desired, the appealing food does make it worth a visit if you prioritize flavor over a flawless bar experience.

The salsa was just some bland tomato sauce with a little chilie and spice, very little flavor. I would have been ok with tacos had it had more cheese and been fried crispy as I requested but this was not good and when asked why it was a taco he told me the cheese was “inside” as if that changed it to a quesadilla i. A taco with a little cheese is still JUST a taco. Lots of cheese and a fried tortilla is what makes a good quesadilla, and with birria the cheese should even be fried on the outside of the tortilla, what he severed me was a greasy soft taco with about a tablespoon of cheese and when dipped into the consommé it just fell apart and made a mess. They didn’t even serve it with lemon or lime. I expected more. This was just OK, not great.

review_text:
Extremely friendly establishment with great Mexican dishes. All wait staff were extremely kind, the kitchen staff were wonderful and cooked everything perfectly, and the menu is very easy to understand.

Monday-Friday 3-5PM is when happy hour is offered for alcoholic beverages and certain appetizers(chicken tenders, nachos, etc).

I have eaten here multiple times and every time I am greeted with both a warm welcome and a great meal.

Denisse was my server and she did everything correctly. She checked on us multiple times during our stay, went over all drink selections(it wasn’t just a “we have Pepsi products”, she went above and beyond even listing off menu drinks like Arnold Palmers they can make). She didn’t pressure us at all, didn’t make us uncomfortable, and was extremely friendly. She also helped us pick the best dessert option I’ve tried so far from this establishment at the end of the meal! Everything you’d want and more.

I ended up ordering the chile rellenos from the à la carte section. Even though they don’t come with meat you can order a side of meat(in my case, I ordered steak), extra cheese, or both! Every visit is tastier than the last. All meals you can request changes/additions and requests are easily met.

For dessert I had a cheesecake chimichanga and it was delivered with the cutest little edible drawing. The perfect end to a perfect night. This place really does go out of their way to make your experience one you will positively remember.

This restaurant offers take out, dine in(indoor and outdoor seating), and delivery(though partners like Grubhub) meal options.

Please support this establishment if you’re thinking about dropping in. Everyone is wonderful and this is definitely a little restaurant you can call home that will have you excited to come back each time. 🫶

(The chiles rellenos ordered are a trio with extra cheese from the Al la carte menu paired with a side of steak for anyone looking to order! The steak is cooked perfectly and I personally layer it on top of the dish.)

Keep trying to give this Location of Los Tres a chance but each time there is a new issue.
Sometimes the food is not great other times the service is terrible, today seemed to be a combination of all of the above.

We actually called in to order and the woman on the phone said she was unable to hear us and asked us to call back which we did immediately only to have them not answer. We tried calling from two separate numbers numerous times and it kept going straight to voicemail.

So then we placed the order online. Upon picking up the orders, we asked for a cup of salsa for each of our two dinners and we were told that we could only have one again even though we had two dinners and there would be an additional charge for the little cup of salsa to go with the chips.

They also didn’t mark the orders so it was extremely hard to figure out who’s who’s.  And then upon looking at my order, I had ordered black beans and I was given refried beans.

So was this exact experience worth the low stars that I am giving the location, no not this exact experience but the accumulation of poor food, poor service and the way the transaction was handled this evening is what prompting my rating and my review. And I think this is the final chance I’m giving to this location.. I’ll drive into Livonia just a few miles away from here on out.

review_text:
Excellent location.  Decor is good, entrance is a little odd, some of the bio murals are ick.  But the reason I'm compelled to review is the service.  The service is bad here.  It has been consistently bad for me, and I've gone at off peak hours when it is not crowded.  Servers do not check back to refill drinks, etc., and you wait and wait and it makes the meal unenjoyable as the time drags on.  For instance, I recently went in the evening, two other tables had people.  I saw three staff sitting at their bar, killing time, while I sat waiting for my bill.  I had my wallet out on the table, my drink empty, salsa empty, utensils across my plate, dishes pushed away from me.  So from across the small room, it was obvious I was waiting for my check.  But, I kid you not, half the time I was in that restaurant was waiting for my check.  After 10-15 minutes, my waiter finally returned, I asked for a drink to go (and it was one that doesn't get free refills, so it was a bonus moneymaker for them) but then back to the waiting game, another 10 min goes by and I give up and just walk to the kiosk where they greet you since there is no register, to force them to deal with me--and the third person to come behind the kiosk did so.  The first two didn't even ask me what I needed or say let me get someone for you.

So I just don't understand this mental block they have.  It's like they never went to a restaurant before, much less run one.  Truly bizarre.  Or just super un-caring.  And being from Texas, I know Mexican restaurants like the back of my hand.  This one may have the worst service I've ever experienced on either side of the border.

Oh, and I just remembered, ordering was weird too.  I said the name of the menu item, as listed on the menu, but then I was asked 20 questions about what I wanted as if I asked for a special order or named something not on the menu or called something on the menu by the wrong name.  So I think it boils down to the personnel not having any professional care or experience, or just some damn common sense about customer service.

I usually don’t leave reviews, but the experience I had tonight was so unbearable, I wouldn’t be doing my due diligence in helping others save their money.

My wife ordered our family’s dinner and I planned on picking it up on my way home from work. When I arrived at the location, I waited 5 minutes to be greeted, there was no one in sight and when any of the employees would see me, they would just stare and keeping doing what they were doing.

When I was finally greeted, the waitress was nice “initially” and apologized for the wait. As she was handing me my food, she asked me was the meals paid for and I said yes. As I was ready to drive off, she comes out yelling stating I didn’t pay for the food. I told her my wife made the order and that I thought everything was taken care of on the phone. She angrily said “we don’t take payments over the phone!” As a worker of the restaurant, it’s your responsibility to check what the status of the meals are and what’s paid/not paid. How am I suppose to know your procedure? This is only my second time at this location.

So I told her I thought the payment was taken care of and it was no problem; I will come in and pay (it wasn’t a big deal). As I went back into the restaurant I was greeted by another employee named Tatyana (she was great and really helpful throughout the entire situation). When I began to pay for my food, I was told that the employee who caught my attention outside kept saying “I got him!”, which alluded that she actually thought that I was actually trying to steal even though I told her multiple times about the situation.

Fast forward, my family is eating and my son wanted chicken tenders and fries. As he was eating his chicken tenders he found a long piece of hair mid bite on his chicken, mind you he’s only 4 years old. I called the restaurant and talked to Tatyana again and she made sure he received a different order (which was the Mac & Cheese). After getting off the phone with Tatyana, my wife alerted me that she had hair in her rice. Now at this point I am angry and disappointed, this was a waste of my hard earned money.

When I went to pick up my son’s food, I told an employee what transpired with my wife’s food as well. At this point my wife was so disgusted she didn’t want any replacement for her food. I asked the employee if the chefs wear any hairnets or use gloves while preparing the food and I was told no. When I returned to my hotel to give my son his remade food, he showed me he had a long piece of hair in his food. We immediately threw all the food away.

Overall, my experience here was pretty great!

Our server, Javier, was amazing! He was polite, personable, and timely. He was definitely the highlight of our dinner!

I went specifically for the birria tacos. I recently had some elsewhere, and had a hankering. They were delicious! Served with a lime wedge and the dip *chef's kiss* And the portion was certainly healthy!

My guest had a fajita burrito. He was somewhat underwhelmed, with his biggest complaint being that the peppers were too sweet, and a little heavy on the lettuce. The tortilla also wasn't big enough to re-roll after adding toppings. However, overall he enjoyed his dish, as well.

We both liked the chips and salsa.

If you're a ginger beer enthusiast like me, don't waste your money on it here. It's bland, very sweet, with little-to-no bite.

The prices for comparable dishes at nearby restaurants was higher. However, part of what you're paying for is the service (again, wonderful!) and the atmosphere.

The restaurant has a cozy feel. They were playing Spanish versions of oldies at a perfect volume. It was fun!

Finally, is like to add that, when they saw I was with a service dog in training, they didn't bat an eye. This isn't the case everywhere. An extra special shout out for that!

🌮 Los Tres Amigos West Jackson came through clutch for us ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

We rolled into Los Tres Amigos West Jackson with a group of about 30 people… parents, coaches, and roughly twenty 14-year-old hockey boys who were loud enough to shake the walls. I figured the staff would either panic or toss us outside. Instead, they handled it like absolute pros.

Service was on point from the second we sat down. The kids were being… well, 14-year-old boys, loud and a little disrespectful at times, and the staff never once got annoyed. They kept smiling, kept moving, and even sang Happy Birthday to one of the boys without hesitation.

Food rundown:
- Queso was legit good.
- I got the fajita burrito. Zero regrets.
- My son crushed his steak quesadilla.
- Everyone around us seemed happy with the tacos.

For a group our size, the food came out fast. Drinks never went empty. The servers were basically sprinting and still kept it all together.

The thing that impressed me most? They split all those checks without messing anything up. That alone deserves a trophy.

Prices were right in line with every other Mexican place around, so no surprises there.

Honestly, huge respect to the staff. They dealt with our chaos better than most places ever could. I’d come back without thinking twice.

I ordered the beef enchiladas dinner. When it arrived, it looked delicious, but after taking a bite of one enchilada, I immediately noticed something was off. I thought maybe it had cooled on the edge of the plate, so I tried the middle one, same result. The meat tasted old and rancid.

I rarely send food back because I worry about retaliation from the kitchen, but my friend insisted I say something. I called the waiter over and explained that I didn’t like the taste of the enchiladas and asked if I could order something else. He seemed confused and called the manager over.

The manager asked if the dish was what I ordered. I confirmed that it was, but explained again that the meat tasted rancid. He took the plate away, and the waiter took my replacement order: shrimp, chicken, and steak fajitas.

When the fajitas arrived, they were completely covered in cheese, and all the proteins were mixed together instead of separated. It honestly looked like leftovers thrown onto a plate and smothered in cheese. I tried a few bites of shrimp and steak but had to stop…it was a mess. No one came back to check whether the replacement dish was satisfactory.

Overall, the food was bad and the service was worse. In hindsight, I should have taken the bland, watered-down salsa as a warning that this “Mexican” restaurant has been toned down for the community. I won’t be returning.

Los Tres Amigos in Michigan Center has become our absolute favorite spot for authentic Mexican food and warm hospitality. From the moment you walk in, the vibrant atmosphere and friendly smiles make you feel right at home.

This was my best friend’s and my first time at Los Tres Amigos, and unfortunately it was a very disappointing experience.

We were seated and given chips and salsa, but no water, and then waited about 20 minutes before a server came back. I also witnessed another table having to chase down a server just to place another order and pay, as they were on a time crunch. The lack of urgency across the floor was very noticeable.

I understand we arrived around 8:30 PM and the restaurant closes at 10 PM, but that does not excuse the level of service we received. The experience overall was exceptionally unacceptable. I will not be returning and would not recommend this location to others.

review_text:
Where do I even begin? This was not a meal. This was a cinematic masterpiece directed by our waiter. From the moment he approached the table, the atmosphere shifted. The lighting seemed warmer. The air felt fresher. I’m fairly certain the background music got louder out of respect.

When he described the specials, I saw my entire life flash before my eyes. I didn’t choose my entrée — the entrée chose me. His timing? Impeccable. His water refills? Telepathic. I blinked and my glass was full. I breathed and the bread basket appeared.

At one point I considered standing up and slow clapping.

If customer service had a Hall of Fame, he would already have a wing. If excellence were a person, it would nervously ask him for tips. I came in hungry and left spiritually fulfilled.

Five stars feels disrespectful. I would rate this experience “astronomical.” NASA should study him. Universities should teach courses about him. Someone write a documentary immediately.

I will be telling my future children about this waiter.

I wanted to take a moment to recognize the outstanding service we received from our waiter Kaiden. From the moment we were seated, they made us feel genuinely welcomed and taken care of. It wasn’t just about taking our order — it was about creating an experience that made our visit memorable.

They greeted us with a warm smile and great energy, immediately setting a positive tone for the meal. They were attentive without being overbearing, checking in at the perfect times and making sure our drinks were always refilled and that we had everything we needed. It was clear they were paying attention to the details.

What really stood out was their knowledge of the menu. They confidently answered our questions, made thoughtful recommendations, and even suggested a dish I probably wouldn’t have ordered on my own — which ended up being one of the best meals I’ve had in a long time. Their enthusiasm about the food made us even more excited to try it.

Even though the restaurant was busy, they never seemed rushed or stressed. They handled multiple tables smoothly and still made us feel like we were their priority. That kind of composure and professionalism is rare and truly appreciated.

Most importantly, they were personable and authentic. They engaged in friendly conversation, remembered small details we mentioned, and made us laugh. It felt less transactional and more like genuine hospitality. You can tell they care about doing a great job and making sure guests leave happy.

Because of their service, our entire experience was elevated. Great food is important, but exceptional service is what makes people want to come back — and this waiter is exactly the kind of employee that builds loyalty.

I hope management recognizes how valuable they are to the team. Employees like this make a lasting impression and represent the restaurant in the best possible way. We will absolutely be returning, and we’ll be hoping to sit in their section again.

review_text:
There are plenty of places to get good Mexican food in this part of Detroit, but if you want seafood, this is the place.

There is a large parking area behind the restaurant, which has a bright blue, colorful sign. Great logo, it would look good on a hat.

Right away you know something is different when instead of getting a dish of salsa with a chip basket you get a dish of diced tomatoes, onions, cilantro with surimi. They let you know right away, this is a sea food place (although they do have other options).

Very well stocked bar, and lots of drink options. Their selections of Micheladas is astounding, featuring some huge options packed with shrimp, crab, etc.

I recommend either looking at the menu ahead of time, or leaving yourself some extra time. It is large, and has many tempting options.

We tried something familiar, Camarones Mexicana (shrimp with tomatoes, onions and just a few jalapeños) and something new to us, a bed of rice with a spicy stew of shrimp, octopus and surimi (we were warned it was spicy, but the balance of heat and flavor was perfect). Everything was excellent.

This is a great place to try an aspect of Mexican cuisine that is often under represented in many restaurants, stop in and try something, you might get a new favorite.

He fell backward and hit the back of his head against the stone wall of the restaurant, and scraped up his back significantly as well. According to my parents, the staff did not seem concerned that this had happened. The actual meal was okay and our server was great, but this really colored our experience and I know my Dad’s back and head still hurt. When we left the restaurant, the bench was still broken, the other next to it just as rusted and (in my opinion) unsafe.

review_text:
From the moment you arrive at Mi Lindo San Blas, it’s clear this is more than just another Mexican restaurant — it’s an experience built around atmosphere, hospitality, and authentic flavor. The exterior immediately stands out with vibrant character and thoughtful architectural detail, while the interior delivers an immersive dining environment that feels warm, energetic, and genuinely transportive. Every aspect of the décor appears intentionally designed to create an inviting and memorable atmosphere, and the restaurant succeeds effortlessly in doing so.

One of the first touches that elevated the experience was the complimentary chips and salsa. While many restaurants treat this as a routine starter, Mi Lindo San Blas delivers freshness and flavor that immediately set the tone for the meal ahead. It’s a small detail, but one that reflects the kitchen’s attention to quality from the very beginning.

The menu itself is impressively expansive, offering an enormous variety of authentic Mexican dishes alongside an equally strong drink selection. Despite the size of the menu, nothing about the experience felt unfocused or overwhelming. Instead, it showcased the restaurant’s versatility and commitment to offering something for every palate.

Service throughout the evening was excellent. Our waitress was exceptionally friendly, attentive, and welcoming without ever feeling intrusive. The staff contributed heavily to the relaxed and enjoyable energy of the restaurant, making the experience feel both comfortable and genuinely hospitable.

The food arrived beautifully presented and cooked with precision. Every dish was packed with bold, authentic flavor, with ingredients tasting fresh and thoughtfully prepared. The kitchen clearly understands balance and seasoning, delivering meals that felt both satisfying and carefully executed rather than rushed or overly commercialized.

The cocktail program deserves recognition as well. The drinks were creative, well-balanced, and expertly poured — visually appealing while still delivering on flavor. It’s evident that the bar program receives the same level of care and consistency as the kitchen.

What ultimately makes Mi Lindo San Blas stand out is its ability to combine strong food, excellent drinks, inviting atmosphere, and warm hospitality into one cohesive experience. In a dining landscape where many restaurants excel in one category while neglecting another, this establishment manages to deliver across the board.

Anyone in the Lincoln Park area looking for authentic Mexican cuisine in a vibrant and memorable setting should absolutely make time to visit Mi Lindo San Blas. My wife and I left thoroughly impressed and are already looking forward to returning.

review_text:
We have ordered delivery (or takeout in one case) a few times from this location. The food is actually quite good and we like the menu variety. There is something all 5 of us like. HOWEVER. There are some major problems with ordering online, either through their website or the DoorDash app. Through their website, you cannot order drinks except for a handful of sodas with a kids meal only. And the bigger problem, that is now deterring me from ordering again, is that through either platform, there is NO way to specify NO CILANTRO. Both my husband and I have the genetic mutation that makes cilantro taste like bitter soap. It makes the whole dish taste extremely unpleasant. And Los Tres Amigos PILES on the cilantro, and it's on everything, especially the dish I most want to order- quesabirria! I tried to pick it all off once and it was impossible. Not only is there no box to check for no cilantro, they also don't allow special instructions so there's no way to add a note, either.

I ordered pickup one time through their website and when I spoke to them about my frustration, their solution was to call to order. For one, I shouldn't have to call just to make a basic request- we're ordering for 5 people so it's not a quick order, and ordering verbally over the phone when it's more than 1 or 2 things just creates more opportunities for mistakes. I also get anxiety about making phone calls, and if I have to make a phone call for something non-essential that I SHOULD be able to do online like everyone else, I'm probably just going to order from somewhere else. I use up my quota of pushing through the anxiety to make calls on calls that are actually important.

Some might say just go dine in store. We have 5 people in our family and deal with major medical conditions and have service dogs. It's a huge production to take our family places, and if I'm ordering from a restaurant, it's probably because I'm an exhausted, overworked mom with brain fog and just need to get dinner on the table for my family. I don't have the energy to drag everyone out to a physical restaurant just because a store doesn't have a checkbox for NO CILANTRO when ordering online.

It's 2026, Los Tres Amigos! I know cilantro is a staple of Mexican food, but thanks to science most people know by now that many people genetically cannot stand the taste of cilantro. You don't want people to eat your food and say it tastes like poison or having their mouth washed out with soap! Thanks to the wonders of technology, the solution to get my business back is extremely simple. All you have to do is add a checkbox for NO CILANTRO to ALL menu options that normally contain it (I know it's possible, because there are a couple of taco items that already have this checkbox) on DoorDash and your website. We already have to pay exorbitant prices to order DoorDash/delivery, this doesn't seem like a big ask.

And please don't just dismiss customer concerns about something like this by telling us to add to our stress and order by phone. I'm tired. I'm supporting my husband through terminal brain cancer treatment while raising our 3 teens/tween who are all neurodivergent (just like their parents). I just want to eat a warm quesabirria with NO CILANTRO.

review_text:
The worst restaurant experience I have ever had.

I placed a takeout order with Ava S. and, after a 30-minute drive home, discovered that my $56 order was poorly prepared, under-seasoned, carelessly thrown together, and partially undercooked. There was even hair wrapped around my jalapeño peppers. The food was so unappetizing that I wouldn't have served it to anyone.

What makes this experience even worse is what I witnessed while waiting for my order. I watched the manager handling fruit garnishes for drinks with his bare hands immediately after touching a yellow and black bag, directly in front of the garnish tray. No gloves, no handwashing—nothing. It was unsanitary and honestly should have been my sign to leave.

When I called simply requesting that my food be replaced, the manager hung up on me. I wasn't asking for a refund, causing a scene, or demanding anything unreasonable. I just wanted the food I paid for to be prepared correctly. Instead, I was met with rudeness and complete disregard for customer service.

I'm not someone who typically leaves negative reviews, but the combination of poor food quality, questionable food-handling practices, and a manager hanging up on a paying customer is unacceptable. Customers deserve to know what they're walking into.

There are plenty of Mexican restaurants in the area that take pride in cleanliness, quality food, and treating customers with respect. Unfortunately, this establishment appears more concerned with taking your money than providing a positive dining experience.

The economy is too expensive for customers to spend their hard-earned money on food that is carelessly prepared and service that is openly disrespectful. Based on what I witnessed, I have serious concerns about the cleanliness standards being followed. If employees are handling drink garnishes with bare hands, it raises legitimate questions about what other health and safety practices may be ignored behind the scenes.

At this point, they can keep the remake. After the way I was treated by management, I have no interest in returning. I will be reporting my concerns to the health department so they can determine whether proper food safety procedures are being followed.

Extremely disappointed, disgusted, and frustrated.
owner_response: We're sorry to hear about your disappointing experience, Roshanna. We're known for our attention to preparation and hygiene, and we regret that we didn't hit the mark during your visit. Our team should have responded better to your concerns and we will work on this. I understand they were probably busy, so I simply ordered through the website instead. Since the website doesn't let you specify tortilla type, I called back to confirm that along with my pickup time.

I arrived at the pickup time they gave me, waited nearly ten minutes, and then my order came out missing one of my three meals.

Both the manager and the hostess just seemed irritated that there was a problem rather than interested in resolving it.

Eventually, I told them I would just try to sort it out with my credit card company and left.

NEVER GO HERE IF YOU HAVE ALLERGIES.

Good stuff:
1. The restaurant got a major makeover and it looks amazing with a good setup.
2. They have Taco Tuesday!
3. The appetizer nachos were awesome; my friend, who didn't even want ground beef, ate half of the shareable portion.
4. The staff is fantastic, which is super important for any business. It's a really positive vibe to chill out in.
5. The mint juleps were good.
6. Taco Tuesday is a great idea with the tacos being super cheap.

Bad stuff (just look at the photos - they say it all):
1. The food. I didn't eat any of the food I ordered, but I still paid for it. My fish (dry) and shrimp tacos were bland just like the refried beans and tacos.
2. The drinks were mixed inconsistently. My $16 drink (it was huge) had way too much mixer, but my friend's drink was tasty. I think I had a strawberry one, but the waiter took it back, and I wasn't charged.
3. Chimichangas. I love chimichangas and was excited for a great meal. I thought the tacos were terrible, but figured chimichangas wouldn't let me down. I was wrong. The chimichanga was drowned in cheese sauce, making it impossible to eat. I even shared a screenshot of it next to the menu.

The Mexican flatbread, was just basically a normal pizza, The burger was very plain, the Chicken dish wasn’t good, then when we got the carne asada with mushrooms, they forgot the mushrooms, and the potatoes that came with the dish were with a sauce that was very unpleasant. They’re trying to do too many things rather than find their identity. Finally, when the bill came, they sent a different associate to collect the bill and they explained “the 80% gratuity was taken off the bill” which we were extremely perplexed by, “then she said the tip is not on the bill”, when I looked at the receipt the gratuity was actually on the bill, for a $450 bill, that should be 100% clarified and not confused when communicating this information. So there’s a lot to be fixed for a new restaurant if they want to succeed.

We're still finding our footing as a newer restaurant, and your honest review helps us understand exactly where we need to tighten things up, so thank you for that. — The Casa Tequila Prime Team

review_text: Tonight I decided to enjoy a meal at a popular restaurant in my area.  Unfortunately I had a terrible experience. The 2 bartenders in front of me looked up and looked away and continued their conversations.  No one spoke to me for another 7-10 mins!  At this point I realized I wasn't going to be helped apparently.  So I started to leave and a server or maybe a manager came and asked if I was the person who ordered tacos. Now frustrated...I replied "no I haven't ordered or been spoken to by anyone but the hostess."  He said oh so do you want to order.  No apology or retrieval of a manager.  Long story long.  This was a discouraging and frustrating experience.  I'm disappointed with the professionalism of the bartenders and frankly the establishment.  I would like to point out that 1 hostess, (whose name I didnt get) was so polite and tried to rectify the situation.  She noticed my frustration and tried to fixed a unsatisfactory situation.
